summary: Lucia Galli is a scholar in Tibetology who earned her doctorate at the University of Oxford and held a post there.

Scherman studied at Breslau and Munich under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and Ernst Kuhn. He served as professor at the University of Munich (PD 1892, eo. Professor 1901, ord. Professor 1916–1933) and director of the Museum Fünf Kontinente (1907–1933).

Luciano Petech studied under Giuseppe Tucci. He was Lector at the University of Allahabad (1938–1946), held the Chair of History of Eastern Asia at Sapienza University of Rome (1955–1984), and served as President of the International Association for Tibetan Studies (~1989–1995).

Lucien Bernot studied at INALCO and EPHE. He served at the CNRS (1947–1964), École Pratique des Hautes Études (1961–1978), and held the professorship of “Sociographie de l’Asie du Sud-Est” at the Collège de France (1979–1985).
Lucien Lévy-Bruhl studied at the École Normale Supérieure and the Sorbonne. He held a post at the University of Paris (~1899–1927) and founded the Institut d'ethnologie.

Lucien Tesnière studied under Antoine Meillet and at Paris, Leipzig, and ENLOV. In linguistics, he held posts at the University of Ljubljana (~1921–1924), University of Strasbourg (1924–1937), and University of Montpellier (1937).

Lucjan Malinowski studied at Uniwersytet Petersburski, Humboldt University of Berlin, University of Jena, and Jagiellonian University. He served as professor of Slavic philology at Jagiellonian University (~1877–1898).
Lucy Annette Jones earned her PhD at Rice University under the supervision of Anne Carolyn Klein and Edith Wyschogrod, working in Tibetology and religious studies.

Ludo Rocher studied at Ghent University and SOAS under Adriaan Scharpé, Jan Gonda, and others. He was Professor at Université libre de Bruxelles (1959–1967) and later Chair and W. Norman Brown Professor at the University of Pennsylvania (1966–2002/2016).

Ludvig Frands Adalbert Wimmer studied under Niels Ludvig Westergaard at the University of Copenhagen (MA, PhD). He remained at Copenhagen as Privatdozent (1871), Docent (1875), and Professor of Nordic Philology (1886–1910).

Ludwig Alsdorf studied under Walther Schubring and Heinrich Lüders at Hamburg and Berlin. He taught at Allahabad (1930–1932), Berlin (1935–1943), and held the chair for Indian history and culture at the University of Hamburg (1950–1978).

Ludwig Bachhofer earned his PhD at the University of Munich under Lucian Scherman. He was a Privatdozent at Munich (1927–1935) before serving as Assistant Professor of Art at the University of Chicago (1935–1965).

Ludwig Diestel studied under Heinrich Ewald (~1845–1847). A scholar of religious studies, he held academic posts at the universities of Greifswald (~1858–1860), Jena (~1860–1862), Bonn (~1862–1872), and Tübingen (~1872–1879).

Ludwig Fritze studied at Lehrerseminar Oranienburg (~1851–1854). Working in Indology, he taught at teacher seminaries in Oranienburg (1861–1871), Zabern (1871–1873), Drossen (1873–1885), and Köpenick (1885–1906).

Ludwig Heinrich Kapff earned his PhD at the University of Tübingen (1826–1829), where he was Privatdozent (1830–1833). He later served as Rector at Karlsgymnasium Heilbronn (1843) and Ephorus at the Evangelische Seminare Maulbronn und Blaubeuren (1854–1869).

Ludwig Heller studied under Franz Kielhorn at Göttingen and habilitated at Greifswald. He worked at the Royal Library of Berlin (1893–1897), University of Tartu (1918), and Greifswald (Privatdozent 1897, ao. Professor 1904, ord. Professor 1920).

Ludwig Lange studied under Karl Friedrich Hermann and Theodor Benfey at Göttingen and Leipzig. He was professor of classical philology at Charles University (1853–1859), University of Giessen (1859), and University of Leipzig (1871; Rektor 1879–1880).

Ludwig Oster was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Richard Pischel (1905–1908) and earned his PhD at Heidelberg University under Christian Bartholomae and Salomon Lefmann (~1908–1911).

Ludwig Poley studied under Franz Bopp in Berlin and later under Eugène Burnouf and Silvestre de Sacy. Working in Indology, he taught at the University of Padua (1866) and served as Privatdozent at the University of Vienna (1867).
Ludwig Ross studied at Kiel University (~1825–1829). He held posts at the National and Kapodistrian University of Athens (1837–1843) and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1845–1859).
